clue.text: What a barrister does is obvious

definitions.meaning: a barrister rises in court and argues a case, standing up to make a reasoned argument
to be self-evident, needing no argument at all

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a lawyer's job is plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a barrister stands up in court in order to reason with the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a conclusion is so logical that nobody could dispute it.

clue.text: Prefer a party with a mix of steak and fish

indicators.note: a mix of tells us the letters of the word steak are jumbled

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish; IDES is its plural

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a dinner party menu of surf and turf.
explanation.definitionFit: To support one faction in a dispute is to favour one party over another.

clue.text: Drug trafficker, having returned, ran Charlie round

indicators.note: having returned says the word ran is turned back to front

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A dealer flees and later comes back to run cocaine (charlie) around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is also slang for cocaine, which suits the drug-dealing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for narcotrafficker, it is slang for someone who deals in illegal drugs.

clue.text: Pointy at one end and blunt at the other? Neat!

definitions.text: Pointy at one end and blunt at the other?
definitions.meaning: a cryptic description of a vessel's outline, pointed bow and squared stern

explanation.surface: A riddle about some oddly shaped object, then an exclamation of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as two words: the outline of a boat, sharp at the bow and flat at the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a nautical idiom for everything tidy and in proper order.

clue.text: Commander and dog are found

definitions.note: plural phrase; the answer, as a verb, matches with a plural subject

parts.note: OC is the abbreviation for Officer Commanding
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: An officer and his dog have been located.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that occur exist or turn up somewhere, as in 'these birds occur in Asia'.

clue.text: Nothing wrong with horsey types coming round day and night just the same then?

definitions.text: day and night just the same then?

indicators.note: coming round says the horse word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: equines are members of the horse family
nothing is zero, the letter O
a cross, X, marks an answer as wrong

explanation.surface: Horses circling at a time when day and night seem identical.
explanation.definitionFit: At these two points in the year the sun crosses the equator and daylight and darkness last roughly twelve hours each.

clue.text: Essence of tasty butcher's special ability

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so the central letter of tasty is taken

parts.note: to butcher is to slaughter, to kill

explanation.surface: The core of a good butcher's shop is a special talent for tasty meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A skill is an expertise or talent, a learned capability someone possesses.

clue.text: Close connection for late shift?

parts.note: nigh means close or near
a tie is a link or connection

explanation.surface: Someone after a handy contact who might get them onto the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work rota, but a shift is also a loose dress, and this one is worn late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple dress, and this garment is the one worn to bed late in the evening.

clue.text: Right cheek going up front flying, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up front means the cheek word rises above the letter for right

parts.note: sauce is impudence, cheek

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside about a flying-front position, perhaps on a rugby pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'going up front' moves SAUCE above R. The definition works by example: a flying one is a supposed alien craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying saucer is the classic UFO, so 'flying' describes one kind of this dish.

clue.text: Measurement of weight lost by jerk

indicators.note: lost by says a piece is dropped from the insult that follows

parts.note: wanker is British slang for an obnoxious jerk

explanation.surface: An idiot has lost some kind of weight measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: The insult is a crude British term for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old Dutch and German unit of liquid capacity, about ten gallons.

clue.text: With stylish clue, pretty much doing nothing unnecessary

parts.note: in means fashionable, stylish

indicators.note: pretty much means nearly all, so the word clue loses its last letter
unnecessary says the zero in doing is surplus and goes

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A setter praising a tight, elegant clue with no wasted words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both prepositions mean together with or containing, as in 'tea, with milk'.

clue.text: Clients with training showing no signs of hesitation exposing former government agency

indicators.note: showing no says both hesitation sounds are removed from the pieces

parts.note: clients are customers
with means and, joining things
exercise is physical training
er is the sound of hesitating; two signs give two of them

explanation.surface: Confident clients at the gym, unmasking an old government department.
explanation.walkthrough: One ER goes from each long word: CUSTOMERS becomes CUSTOMS and EXERCISE becomes EXCISE.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British department collecting duties and taxes until merging with the Inland Revenue in 2005.

clue.text: Call Latvian on the phone to provide hair styling

parts.note: to ring is to call by telephone

indicators.note: words heard on the phone are heard rather than read, so the Baltic word is taken by sound

parts.note: a Lett is a person from Latvia

explanation.surface: Ringing a Latvian stylist to book a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiralling curl, a way of dressing the hair.

clue.text: Passenger added clause

definitions.meaning: someone carried along, on a horse, a bike or a bus
an extra provision tacked onto a contract or bill

explanation.surface: A traveller and a bit of legal small print.
explanation.definitionFit: One who travels on a vehicle; also an amendment appended to a legislative bill.

clue.text: Back in, staggered about. Shocking!

indicators.note: about says the word for staggered wraps around the shock treatment

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, is shock treatment

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled back into the house, and what a shock it was!
explanation.definitionFit: A politician returned to office by voters is back in power.

clue.text: See 12
Little girl's bad mood creates problem with dogs

parts.note: Di, a short form of Diana, with the possessive making DI'S
a temper is an angry mood

explanation.surface: A small girl's tantrum causes trouble with the family dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: This viral disease infects dogs and other animals, an ailment canine owners dread.

clue.text: Ken lacking bliss, they say

definitions.meaning: ken is knowledge, so this is a want of knowledge
the proverb holds that not knowing is bliss

explanation.surface: Poor Ken is short of happiness, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name; it is the Scots word for knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means want of knowledge, and the proverb says that state is bliss.

clue.text: Incredibly, I see beggars throwing silver back — and they keep pestering!

indicators.note: incredibly suggests the letters are taken in an unbelievable new order
throwing out signals that some letters are cast away from the pool
back says the symbol for silver is reversed

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Beggars hurling back coins and continuing to hassle passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GA (AG, from 'silver', turned round by 'back') out of I SEE BEGGARS; 'Incredibly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Besiegers surround a place and keep up harassing attacks, a fair loose sense of pestering.

clue.text: Endorse record that hasn't had the attention it should

definitions.text: that hasn't had the attention it should
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun

parts.note: to endorse is to back or support
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Signing off a record that nobody had properly looked at.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of work left undone and still waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: Ecumenical council takes part in heresy, no doubt

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A church gathering joins in condemning heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy; an ecumenical one draws together the whole Christian church.

clue.text: I originally wanted surrealist painter to host festival

indicators.note: to host says the painter's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of wanted

explanation.surface: Someone longing for Salvador Dali to throw a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, celebrated each autumn.

clue.text: Speak well of company men managing director retained

indicators.note: retained says the other pieces keep the men inside them

explanation.surface: A firm's staff praising the boss who was kept on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company men' reads as one phrase, corporate loyalists, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone formally is to speak highly of them.

clue.text: Geochronological peak, within two degrees? That's hot!

indicators.note: within says the peak letter goes inside the pair of degrees
two says the degree abbreviation is used twice

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

indicators.note: in a down entry the peak of a word is its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A geologist's peak dated within a couple of degrees: a hot find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degrees' looks like temperature, but it means academic qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock beneath the earth's crust is extremely hot, the source of lava.

clue.text: In brief, doctor died before he got to marry Liz

definitions.note: an abbreviated doctorate, the qualification of a doctor

parts.note: Prince Philip married Princess Elizabeth, later Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: An obituary: the doctor died before he could wed his Liz.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor of Philosophy, shortened, is the Oxford title for a doctoral degree.

clue.text: Intellectual being referred to in EastEnders a feature one might raise?

indicators.note: spoken in the Cockney of the BBC soap EastEnders, set in London's East End, where the initial H is dropped

parts.note: an intellectual is a highbrow, which a Cockney says as 'ighbrow, dropping the aitch

explanation.surface: An intellectual mentioned on the London soap opera EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops an initial H, so 'being referred to in EastEnders' makes HIGHBROW come out as 'IGHBROW, sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift this arch of facial hair to show surprise or doubt.

clue.text: Place where the chicks are all high?

definitions.text: Place where the chicks are all high?

parts.words: Place where the chicks are all high?
parts.note: chicks suggests young women and high suggests drugs, but these are baby birds in a lofty nest

explanation.surface: A party venue where the girls are all stoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, built on a cliff or treetop.

clue.text: Sparks up joint, which attracts the attention of sailors

definitions.text: which attracts the attention of sailors

parts.note: to spark up is to light, as with a cigarette
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Someone lights a spliff that draws the eye of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon warns and guides mariners, like a floating lighthouse.

clue.text: Authentic section finally introduced by organ

definitions.note: noun, while the answer is an adjective meaning of the kidney organ

indicators.note: introduced says a letter is put into the word for authentic

parts.note: real means authentic

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of section

explanation.surface: A genuine passage played on the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the kidneys, the bodily organ named here loosely.

clue.text: Unravel red flag, possibly leading to complaint

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Taking apart a red warning flag might make someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: This viral illness, mononucleosis, is a complaint in the sense of an ailment.
